books.section: Great Depression and the New Deal (1929-1939)

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 23, and Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 9, Topic 7.10: When Roosevelt took office in March 1933, banks were failing as frightened depositors withdrew their money. He closed all banks for four days so the government could inspect them, and most reopened by March 15. The Banking Act of 1933 then created the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, which insured individual deposits. In the same first Hundred Days, Congress created the Civilian Conservation Corps, which gave young men work on forest and conservation projects; the Agricultural Adjustment Administration, which paid farmers to grow less so prices would rise; and the National Industrial Recovery Act, which set industry codes for wages, hours, and prices and displayed a Blue Eagle poster in shops that complied.

stem: The Civilian Conservation Corps described in the passage best shows which aim of the First New Deal?

options.text: Giving unemployed young men work that helped families
Paying farmers to cut back on production
options.misconception: Paying farmers to grow less was the work of the Agricultural Adjustment Administration, not the CCC.

options.text: Insuring the savings of ordinary bank depositors
options.misconception: Insuring bank deposits was the work of the FDIC, not the CCC, which gave young men outdoor work.

options.text: Breaking up large corporations into smaller firms
options.misconception: The New Deal did not break up large corporations; the CCC put young men to work on conservation projects.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the CCC gave young men work on forest and conservation projects, and most of their small pay was mailed home to their families.
rationales.B: Background from the books: paying farmers to cut production was the AAA, while the CCC employed young men on outdoor conservation work.
rationales.C: Background from the books: the FDIC insured bank deposits; the CCC was a jobs program for young men, not a banking reform.
rationales.D: Background from the books: breaking up corporations was a Progressive-era trust policy, not a CCC aim; the CCC was about jobs and conservation.
rationales.general:
1. The passage places the CCC in the first Hundred Days, alongside banking and farm relief.
2. Its job was work for young men on forest and conservation projects.
3. The books add that most of their pay went home to their families.
4. So the CCC joined relief for the jobless with help for their households.
Remember: a jobs program can serve two aims at once, work for the worker and support for the family.
